root_idea.summary: The root exhibits three broad orientations: loss of sharpness or force, enclosure or surrounding, and a bodily member. These develop into meanings of dullness, fatigue, dependence, encompassing totality, collateral relation, and crown-like encirclement.
root_idea.development: The loss-of-edge branch yields dullness, weakness, fatigue, and burden; the enclosing branch yields total inclusion, collateral kinship, and crown or surrounding formations. Related lexical developments also include anatomical and figurative extensions.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Distinct Quranic noun meaning a burden or dependent.
The occurrence at 4:91 is the temporal conjunction كُلَّمَا represented by a separate QAC segmentation.

senses.definition: A deceased person who leaves neither parent nor offspring; by extension, the inheritance situation defined by that absence.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in inheritance discourse; the term may refer to the deceased person or to the estate and succession case associated with the absence of direct ascendants and descendants.

senses.definition: The collateral heirs of a person who leaves neither parent nor offspring—heirs other than the direct parent or child.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in inheritance discourse for heirs connected through a collateral relationship rather than the direct parent-child line.

senses.definition: A burden, especially a dependent person who must be supported.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction كَلٌّ عَلَى مَوْلَاهُ, the term describes someone or something burdensome to a supporting patron.

senses.definition: The whole or complete extent of a thing, including all of its relevant parts or states; fully or completely.
senses.usage_conditions: Used with a noun, pronoun, or an understood complement when the emphasis is on the entirety or complete degree of a thing or state.

senses.definition: Every, each, or all: encompassing the members or kinds of a set.
senses.usage_conditions: Used with a definite plural, a pronoun, a singular indefinite, or an understood complement; the construction may be distributive or collective according to context.
In a negative clause followed by an exception, كُلٌّ means “any one,” as in the Quranic negative–exception construction.

senses.definition: Whenever; every time that; as often as.
senses.usage_conditions: Introduces a recurring temporal condition or circumstance, normally followed by a clause describing what happens on each occurrence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become dim, dull, or less clear, especially of sight.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I verbal use applied to the sight or visual faculty.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become fatigued, weary, or weak, with resulting inability to perform an act.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person, animal, or limb in constructions describing fatigue, weakness, or incapacity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To set the teeth on edge.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression for the effect of acidic or sour food or drink; the Form IV expression takes the teeth as its object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become blunt and unable to cut, especially of a sword or similar implement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of an edged tool whose cutting sharpness has been lost.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To adorn or be adorned with gems or jewels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: كَلَّلَ is the active Form II verb; مُكَلَّلٌ is the corresponding passive participial description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Weak or faint, as of lightning; dull or lacking sharpness, as of a tongue.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived adjective used for diminished force, brightness, or sharpness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The utmost degree of a quality in an emphatic construction.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in an emphatic appositional expression such as “the learned one, the entirety of the learned”; this is a Classical Arabic intensifying construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Whatever; anything that.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical use distinct from the temporal conjunction “whenever.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Whoever.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A compound indefinite expression referring to any person who satisfies the following condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Universal, general, or relating to the whole; as a substantive, a universal or that which comprises particulars; كُلِّيَّةٌ denotes universality or totality.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in contrast with the particular or جزئيّ; the forms may be adjectival, substantive, or abstract.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The five predicables of logic: genus, species, difference, property, and accident.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical logical expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The seventeenth lunar mansion, associated with the head of Scorpio; also the group of three bright stars in or before that region.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An astronomical term whose naming is connected with encirclement or a crown-like arrangement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The border of flesh surrounding the nail.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical expression using the image of a surrounding crown or rim.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cloud that circles or surrounds a place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or descriptive use based on surrounding or encircling.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An orphan, understood as one requiring support.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported Classical usage motivated by the person’s dependence on a supporter; it is distinct from the Quranic burden construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To carry.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported usage attributed to some speakers; its relation to the comparison with نكل is uncertain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Distant collateral kin, especially remote cousins, considered as heirs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical inheritance specialization narrower than the general collateral-heir use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The chest.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A bodily term tentatively related in the lexical tradition to the surrounding or supported-body branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Short.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate, rare lexical use reported in the Classical tradition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To laugh.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the expression describing a woman laughing; the subject in that example does not restrict the verb to women.

cautions: كَلَالَةٌ is used in the supplied Quran-focused evidence both for the deceased or inheritance situation lacking a parent and child and for the collateral heirs; these are presented as separate but related senses.
The negative–exception sense of كُلٌّ is illustrated at the independently supplied QAC location 38:14; the historical printed citation in the lexical evidence is not converted into a modern location.
A reported comparison of كَلَّلَ with نكل in the root discussion does not have a securely recoverable sense in the supplied evidence.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The exact meaning intended by the comparison كَلَّلَ مِثْلُ نَكَلَ in the Maqayis discussion remains unresolved; the separately reported 'to carry' usage is retained as a qualified Classical meaning rather than treated as certain.
